section_summary.extract_value: Abstract describes two studies. Study 1 used a cross-sectional sample of female UK students (n = 215, 17–30 years) and found appearance goals were indirectly, negatively associated with body image via introjected regulation. Study 2 (n = 165, 18–27 years) experimentally manipulated guilt and appearance goals and found guilt increased post-test body anxiety for participants in the guilt condition.
section_summary.evidence_source: Study 1 investigated these relationships within a cross-sectional sample of female UK students (n = 215, 17–30 years). Appearance goals were indirectly, negatively associated with body image due to links with introjected regulation. Study 2 experimentally tested this pathway, manipulating guilt relating to exercise and appearance goals independently and assessing post-test guilt and body anxiety (n = 165, 18–27 years). The guilt manipulation significantly increased post-test feelings of guilt, and these increases were associated with increased post-test body anxiety, but only for participants in the guilt condition.
